explanation.keyIdea: A fretted note sounds clearly when the finger lands just behind the fret wire, presses only as hard as needed, and the picking hand strikes the intended string cleanly.

lessons.title: Read guitar maps
lessons.focus: Chord-box orientation, TAB lines and fret numbers
learningObjectives: Explain or demonstrate the main idea: chord-box orientation, tab lines and fret numbers.
Perform the target task accurately at a comfortable, controlled tempo.

explanation.keyIdea: Guitar TAB is a map of strings and fret numbers. The top line represents the thinnest string (high E); a number tells you which fret to play, and 0 means an open string. Staff notation is an optional parallel way to name pitch and rhythm.
explanation.plainLanguage: This lesson focuses on chord-box orientation, tab lines and fret numbers. Treat the written checkpoint as an observable target, not a deadline. First understand the sound or movement, then practise a small part, then return to the musical whole.

demonstrationOrReference.referenceSuggestion: Use a clear, slow demonstration of chord-box orientation, tab lines and fret numbers from a reputable guitar-learning source or your own view of the fretboard. Compare the demonstration with the step-by-step guide here; no paid-course video or protected tab is reproduced.
steps: Read the six TAB lines as the six strings; check the tuning labels before playing.
Read numbers from left to right. Play stacked numbers together; play separated numbers in sequence.
For a chord diagram, read the vertical lines as strings and horizontal spaces as frets; dots show where fingers go and an X/O indicates muted/open strings.
